title: What do the design and distribution obligations (RG 274) mean for staff training?
description: How the design and distribution obligations in Part 7.8A and ASIC's RG 274 treat staff training as part of reasonable steps, and what evidence to keep.
shortAnswer: The design and distribution obligations (DDO) in Part 7.8A of the Corporations Act 2001 require issuers and distributors of financial products to take reasonable steps so products reach consumers in the target market. Regulatory Guide 274 (RG 274) from the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) says ASIC will consider whether distributors gave staff sufficient training and assessed their skills, including on product attributes and target markets, not only sales conduct.
keyTakeaways: The obligations have applied since October 5, 2021 to issuers and distributors of financial products for retail clients.
Distributors must take reasonable steps that will, or are reasonably likely to, result in distribution consistent with the target market determination (s994E(3)).
RG 274 lists training as a factor ASIC considers: whether staff received sufficient training and had their skills assessed.
Issuers may need to give distributors tailored information, which can include training or scripts, and may need to provide training when distribution goes wrong.
Distributors must report significant dealings outside the target market to the issuer within 10 business days, so frontline staff need to recognize them.
appliesTo: Issuers of financial products that require a target market determination
Distributors, including AFS licensees, credit licensees and their representatives engaging in retail product distribution conduct
Sales, contact centre, broker and product governance staff
Senior management responsible for product governance arrangements

sections.heading: What do the design and distribution obligations require?

blocks.text: The obligations require issuers to design products for a defined target market and require issuers and distributors to take reasonable steps so products reach that market. ASIC's [RG 274](https://asic.gov.au/regulatory-resources/find-a-document/regulatory-guides/rg-274-product-design-and-distribution-obligations/), issued in its current form on September 10, 2024, explains that the obligations were introduced by the Treasury Laws Amendment (Design and Distribution Obligations and Product Intervention Powers) Act 2019 and have applied from October 5, 2021.

blocks.caption: Core obligations in Part 7.8A (summarized from RG 274 Tables 1 and 2)
head: Obligation
Who
Corporations Act
rows: Make a target market determination (TMD) with the required content
Not distribute unless a TMD has been made (or is not required)
Take reasonable steps so distribution is consistent with the TMD
Notify the issuer of significant dealings inconsistent with the TMD within 10 business days
Keep records of distribution information, including complaints

blocks.text: ASIC also has a stop order power under Part 7.8A (s994J) to stop the issue or distribution of a product where the obligations are not met. The obligations sit in the [Corporations Act 2001](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A00818/latest/text); this summary reflects them as at September 2026.

sections.heading: Where does RG 274 mention staff training?

blocks.text: RG 274 treats training as one of the factors ASIC considers when deciding whether a distributor has taken reasonable steps. Table 6 of the [published guide](https://download.asic.gov.au/media/etgm1amc/rg274-published-10-september-2024.pdf) says: "We will take into account whether a distributor has given staff involved in distribution operations sufficient training and has assessed the staff members' skills to perform the required duties."

The same entry adds that a distributor "should consider whether specific training is required for staff to understand the key product attributes and the target market for certain products, in addition to training about appropriate sales conduct", and that this training could often be built into existing training, particularly where continuing professional development requirements already apply.
Training also appears in three other places:

items: **Governance culture (RG 274.55):** product governance arrangements need "staff at all levels, including senior management" to understand them and be committed to them.

**Issuer information to distributors (Table 4):** issuers should consider distributors' likely knowledge and what form best meets their needs, "which could include discussions, training, or scripts as appropriate".

**Remediation examples (RG 274.148):** where a distributor promotes a product in a way that risks sales outside the target market, the issuer could, among other steps, "provide training if necessary".

sections.heading: What do distribution staff need to know and do?

blocks.text: Frontline staff need to understand who a product is for, recognize when a customer is unlikely to be in the target market, follow the distribution conditions, and escalate complaints and possible significant dealings. The table below is an original, illustrative mapping of DDO duties to learning outcomes and evidence.

blocks.caption: Illustrative DDO training map for a distributor
head: Duty
Learning outcome
Assessment evidence
rows: Explains the target market, key attributes and exclusions of each product sold
Product knowledge check before being allowed to sell the product
Applies the conditions, such as eligibility questions or channel restrictions, on every sale
Call or file quality review against the conditions
Assessing whether a consumer is likely in the target market (RG 274.175 to 274.189)
Asks the questions the distribution process requires and acts on the answers
Observed sales or recorded call sampling
Recognizes and escalates dealings materially outside the target market
Records every complaint about a product so it reaches issuer reporting
Complaints data reconciled to product reporting
Understands how remuneration rules prevent pressure to sell outside the target market

blocks.text: For advice staff and relevant providers, the [financial adviser education and CPD requirements](/regulations/financial-adviser-education-and-cpd-requirements) include a regulatory compliance category that can carry DDO content. Staff giving general advice are covered by [RG 146](/regulations/asic-rg-146-training-requirements).

sections.heading: What training responsibilities do issuers have?

blocks.text: Issuers are not required to train distributors' staff in every case, but RG 274 expects them to consider whether distributors can meet the conditions and to supply information in a form distributors can use. Table 4 lists the distributor's resources, internal controls, past conduct, experience with the target market and "competence to distribute the financial product to the target market" as relevant factors when selecting distributors.

An issuer's own staff also need training: product design, TMD drafting, review triggers and monitoring of distributor data all require specific capability. The [guide to mapping training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations) shows how to assign these duties to roles.

sections.heading: How should training change when a TMD changes?

blocks.text: When an issuer revises a TMD, distributors must distribute consistently with the most recent TMD, so product training has to follow each revision. A practical control is to tie each product module to the TMD version it reflects:

items: Record the TMD version and date that each product module and assessment was built from.
When the issuer notifies a new TMD, identify every module, script and question that references the old target market or conditions.
Update content and reassess affected staff before or promptly after the new TMD applies.
Keep the version history so a sale can be traced to the training the staff member held at that date.

blocks.text: The guide on [updating training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change) applies the same method to legislative change.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry can hold each product's target market, key attributes and distribution conditions as structured concepts linked to the roles that sell the product and the questions that assess them. When a TMD changes, the affected modules and assessments are identified from those links, and each staff member's record shows which TMD version they were assessed against.

faqs.q: Does RG 274 require a specific DDO course?
faqs.a: No. RG 274 does not prescribe a course. ASIC says it will take into account whether distribution staff received sufficient training and had their skills assessed, and whether specific training on product attributes and target markets was needed. The content and format are for the distributor to decide.

Not necessarily. RG 274 says distributors should consider whether specific training is needed for staff to understand key product attributes and the target market, in addition to training about appropriate sales conduct.

faqs.q: Do DDO apply to general advice and execution only sales?
faqs.a: Retail product distribution conduct includes dealing in the product, giving a disclosure document or PDS, and providing financial product advice (RG 274.29), so general advice and execution only sales are covered. Personal advice is excluded conduct, so obligations such as s994E(3) reasonable steps do not apply to it (RG 274.31).

faqs.q: What records show DDO training was adequate?
faqs.a: Useful records include the product modules and the TMD version each reflects, assessment results before staff were allowed to sell, quality review results against distribution conditions, and escalation and complaint logs showing staff applied the training.
